---
title: "About"
---
Terramechanics Reference Data collects measured soil tests and the setup of each, so that a simulation of the same test can be compared with the measurement. It is maintained by the Simulation-Based Engineering Laboratory (SBEL), University of Wisconsin-Madison.

## Sources

The tests come from published reports. Those in this release come from the Bendix "Lunar Module (LM) Soil Mechanics Study" (NASA, 1968, report AM-68-1), in two volumes: Volume I, Sections II to V (soil selection and the basic tests, the drag and impact tests, and the 1/6-scale Lunar Module model drops) and Volume II, Appendices A to C (soil specifications, sonic moduli and the full direct shear program). NASA's technical reports server lists it for public distribution, with public use permitted. The page images on this site come from it, courtesy of NASA; the report itself is linked, not copied: [Volume I](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19680021852) and [Volume II](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19680021853) (D-054). The [Sources](../sources/index.qmd) page lists the 7 reports acquired for the collection and the leads being considered.

## How the numbers were read and checked

Most numbers in the reports exist only as printed figures. Each figure whose numbers are in the data was read twice, separately, by two readers (the AI systems Claude and Codex), each from the scanned page and without seeing the other's reading. In some early batches both readers also saw notes from an earlier step, so those readings were not fully independent; the review record of each batch says where. A script compared the two readings point by point. Where they disagreed, a fresh reading of the page, made without knowing which reading was whose, settled it, or the point was left marked as unsettled. Then student reviewers compare a sample of the points with the scan, and every check they make is recorded.

Every point carries:

1. its source: the report, the figure or table, the printed page and the page of the PDF file;
2. a reading bound: how precisely it could be read from the printed figure (not the scatter of the experiment, which the reports rarely give);
3. a status word that says which of the checks above it passed (see the [Glossary](../glossary/index.qmd#status-words)).

Values are given in SI units, with the printed value kept beside them. On the [Figures](../figures/index.qmd) page both readings are drawn over the scanned page, so any point can be checked by eye. The detailed rules are in [Methods](../methods/index.qmd).

## Known limitations

1. The numbers are read from scans more than half a century old; each point's reading bound says how precisely.
2. The reports rarely give the uncertainty of the experiments themselves. Tests repeated on similar beds show how much results can differ.
3. Some setups are incomplete: the depth of a soil bed, or how it was placed, is often not printed. Each test page lists what is missing as choices left to the user.
4. Only a sample of the points is checked by a person; each test page says how many.
5. Where the report contradicts itself (a test labeled differently in two figures), the record says so rather than choosing. The open questions, under [Project records](../records/index.qmd), list every such case.

## Using the data

1. Find a test: [Find a test](../experiments/index.qmd) lists every record; each test's page gives its setup, its plot and its source pages.
2. Download its values: the buttons under the plot give the points in SI (CSV) and how they were read (JSON); [Download](../downloads/index.qmd) gives the index files.
3. Trace a number: each value names the report, figure or table, printed page and PDF page; the scanned page is on the test's page, and the [Figures](../figures/index.qmd) page draws the readings over it.
4. Cite it: the release used, the record id, and the page of the report (each test's page shows how).

## Contribute, cite, follow the work

1. [Contribute](../contribute/index.qmd): data from new tests, scripts that run virtual experiments, corrections.
2. [Download](../downloads/index.qmd): the files, the license and how to cite.
3. [Project records](../records/index.qmd): decisions, the review record and the open questions.
